ety.text: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *áno- Proto-Indo-European *-h₁ Proto-Indo-European *né-h₁der. Latin ne From Proto-Indo-European *né-h₁ (“that way, so”), which consists of *áno- (“yonder”, pronomial stem, distal) + *-h₁ (modal and instrumental suffix). Cognate with Ancient Greek νή (nḗ, “yes, indeed”) and Proto-Germanic *-nā (emphatic suffix after adverbs) which features in Icelandic svona (“so”), hérna (“here”), and þarna (“there”). The same pronominal stem is also present in the words enim (“for; truly”), nempe (“indeed”), and nam (“for”).
From nōdō (“to knot, tie in a knot”) + -bilis, from nōdus (“knot”).

ety.text: If correct, ouls shows the use of the digraph "ou", which is puzzling since long /uː/ is etymologically unexpected for this word. Lindsay argues that "ouls" is not the original spelling in this passage, suggesting that the manuscript forms may result either from misreading of an attempted correction of an original *ols to uls, or incorrect emendation of a misspelling vis.
